files.reason: default_controller() looks for microcoder only beside the canonicalized exe (exe_dir/microcoder), then in ~/.openagents/bin. It never checks the app-bundle layout (Contents/Helpers/openagents to Contents/MacOS/microcoder), so the shipped CLI falls back to a stale installed engine that lacks Access::Toolchains. Add controller_candidates(exe, home) returning, in order: exe_dir/microcoder, exe_dir/../MacOS/microcoder, home/.openagents/bin/microcoder. default_controller then takes the first candidate that is_file(). Add unit tests in the existing tests module (starts about line 2010).
controller() calls autostart::default_controller() after the OPENAGENTS_CODER_CONTROLLER override. It should keep working unchanged if the signature of default_controller stays the same.
Puts microcoder at Contents/MacOS/microcoder and openagents at Contents/Helpers/openagents. The new candidate must match this layout; no change expected.

answer.likely_change: In crates/coder/src/task/autostart.rs, replace the body of default_controller() with a lookup over a new controller_candidates(exe: Option<&Path>, home: Option<&Path>) -> Vec<PathBuf>. The candidates are the microcoder beside the exe, the bundle sibling ../MacOS/microcoder (for Contents/Helpers/openagents), and ~/.openagents/bin/microcoder, in that order. The first candidate that is a file wins, so a bundled CLI uses the engine that shipped with it. Local.rs keeps calling default_controller unchanged.
acceptance: A CLI at Contents/Helpers/openagents with microcoder at Contents/MacOS/microcoder resolves to the bundled microcoder.
When no beside-exe microcoder exists, the resolver falls back to ~/.openagents/bin/microcoder.
OPENAGENTS_CODER_CONTROLLER still overrides everything in coder::task::local::controller().
When no candidate exists, the error still names where it looked and suggests --controller.
A regression test covers controller_candidates ordering and the bundle layout.
